calls.head: Iron sharpens iron
calls.body: The Panthers are one of the league’s best for the power play, but the Stars are one of the best at the penalty kill. Our lean: the Panthers’ power play wins out. Power plays usually beat kills in these spots. The Stars take a lot of penalties and the Panthers draw plenty of them, so their power play should get its chances.

calls.beyond: Florida usually gets some of the league’s least dangerous shots. Even by those standards, this was a night of harmless shots: a 3.7% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 5.9% and a league average of 6.3%. A team strays this far about once every 50 games.

DAL.head: We leaned Dallas’s way (56%), and they came through.

surprises.head: Both teams played to type
surprises.body: Nothing in this game strayed far from how these two usually play: the shot share, the quality of chances, special teams, hitting, ice time and goaltending all landed inside their normal night-to-night range.

story.head: Robertson ends it in overtime
paras: Matthew Tkachuk got the scoring started for the Panthers on the power play early in the second, his 700th NHL point. Wyatt Johnston tied it up for Dallas just under five minutes later. Jason Robertson won it just under three minutes into overtime.

The chances were close to even, so this one could have gone either way. Casey DeSmith made 25 saves for the Stars, and Akira Schmid stopped 20 of 22 at the other end. The Stars improved to 12-6-2, fourth in the Central, while the Panthers fell to 12-7-3, fifth in the Atlantic.

items.text: The Panthers’ three-game winning streak is over.
Matthew Tkachuk has a point in eight straight games.
Sam Reinhart extended his point streak against Dallas to seven games.

The Stars won without Miro Heiskanen, Oskar Bäck, Lian Bichsel and others. Taking into account how much value each of these missing players usually adds, only the Avalanche and the Mammoth were missing more at the time.
